attempts.paper_title: Network Homeostasis and State Dynamics of Neocortical Sleep
attempts.entry_title: Network homeostasis and state dynamics of neocortical sleep (Watson et al. 2016)
attempts.summary: The paper's central finding, that sleep evens out pyramidal cell firing rates, with fast cells slowing and slow cells speeding up across sleep and within nonREM packets, held up in the CRCNS copy of the full data set. State durations, firing rates by state and UP/DOWN state durations mostly matched too. Not reproduced were most of the sub-state effects of Figure 5, such as rate changes across microarousals or REM between packets, the decline of spindle and UP/DOWN incidence over sleep, and the rate-group correlations of Figure 2F. For the microarousal effects, the deposited microarousals do not match the paper's (434 within sleep against 790). The DANDI copy is a subset and lacks the lab's sleep sub-state intervals.
attempts.description: Tests the findings of Watson, Levenstein, Greene, Gelinas and Buzsaki (2016) on both of the paper's datasets, DANDI:000041 (22 NWB files of spikes, LFP and Awake, Non-REM and REM states) and CRCNS:fcx-1 (the lab's 27 session folders with spikes, LFP, state intervals, UP/DOWN states, spindles and motion). It covers the data set's counts and state durations, firing rates by state, burst index, autocorrelograms, synchrony, UP/DOWN and spindle statistics, rate changes over sleep, within nonREM episodes and packets, and across sleep sub-state triplets.

findings.statement: DANDI:000041 holds 22 of the paper's 27 sessions. The three sessions of rat B22 (CRCNS 20140526_277um, 20140527_421um, 20140528_565um) and the ACC probes of Dino 061914 and 062014 (52 and 24 units) are not in it, so it holds 10 of 11 rats, 850 of 995 pE and 95 of 126 pI cells.

Dino-061914 in DANDI:000041 has no LFP; the release notes say the lab's source file does not divide into whole channels at 128. The CRCNS .eeg of both Dino 061914 folders divides into 142 channels, which the .xml gives and the stream's own autocorrelation confirms.

DANDI:000041 holds only Awake, Non-REM and REM epochs. The paper's analysis units (WAKE, SLEEP and WAKE-SLEEP cycles, packets, MAs, WAKE interruptions, nonREM and REM episodes), its UP/DOWN states and spindles, and the motion and EMG signals, all in CRCNS:fcx-1, are not in it, and its only ElectricalSeries is the 1250 Hz LFP, so no EMG can be derived from a wideband signal. Built here from the epochs by Table S1's rules they differ from the lab's, 47 cycles against 51, one session without a cycle, 181 MAs in cycles against 434, median packet 144 s against 111 s, median REM episode 64 s against 98 s.

In 7 DANDI sessions whose spike trains are identical, train for train, to the CRCNS stable units, the cell_type labels differ from the lab's _CellIDs (EAll and IAll), for example BWRat20-101513 with 63 pE and 3 pI against 60 and 6. The CRCNS labels give the paper's 995 and 126; the DANDI labels describe cells the paper classed otherwise.

The DANDI unit tables of Dino-072314 and Dino-072414 hold 10 and 15 units more than the CRCNS stable set (26 against 16, 61 against 46), Dino-061814 one more, and Dino-072114 16 units of which 13 match the 18 CRCNS units. paper_notes.statement: The paper reports 790 MAs (median 15.9 s, 0.32 per minute, 9.1% of SLEEP). The deposited _WSRestrictedIntervals hold 2130 MAs, of which 434 lie within the SLEEP of the 51 WAKE-SLEEP cycles (median 11.0 s, 0.18 per minute, 3.7% of SLEEP), none in another scored SLEEP, 26 in a scored WAKE and 1670 outside any scored SLEEP or WAKE (BWRat21_121613 alone has 349 of these); 264 lie between two packets. Every group has a median near 11 s and none counts 790. Which MAs the paper counted is not stated. Question for the paper's authors.

Spindle incidence is 1.94 per minute in the Results and 0.049 Hz (2.94 per minute) in Table S1; the deposited spindles give 2.85 per minute of nonREM pooled and 2.95 as the median over sessions, which agrees with Table S1. The deposited spindles also match Table S1's count (5203), duration, frequency and amplitude.

Table S1 gives a WAKE-SLEEP episode duration of 5918 +- 125 s; the deposited cycles give a median of 4214 s, while every other duration in Table S1 (WAKE 1192, SLEEP 2421, nonREM episode 297, REM episode 98, REM latency 647 s) is matched exactly by the same intervals.

The UP/DOWN detection's LowGammaPower epochs are 'power in the 100 Hz+ range below 0.5 SD below the mean'. On the LFP's linear power that level is almost never reached (the 5th percentile is -0.40 SD in BWRat17-121912), so the band, smoothing and transform must differ from a plain reading. This attempt used log power of 100-400 Hz, smoothed over 25 ms; with it the medians match (0.471 and 0.193 s) but the counts exceed Table S1 by 37% and 31%. Question for the paper's authors, the band, smoothing and scale of this rule.

The sampling unit of the correlations against normalized time (per packet, per 10 s bin, or bins averaged over episodes) is not stated, and outcomes depend on it, the CV over SLEEP decreases with p = 0.0022 per packet but p = 0.19 in 10 s bins on CRCNS, and spindle and UP/DOWN incidence trends differ between readings. Question for the paper's authors, which unit Figures 3 and 4 use.

Questions for the paper's authors. (1) Whether the burst index is the proportion of ISIs of 15 ms or less (Supplemental Experimental Procedures) or the fraction of spikes with such an ISI (Results). (2) The model and fit range of the autocorrelogram decay exponent. (3) How triplets are formed, which WAKE counts between two packets, and whether REM-packet-REM triplets allow an arousal after the first REM. (4) Whether the motion signal was z-scored before the movement correlation, and which measure of movement was used. (5) How the WAKE sextiles are computed for cells recorded over several cycles, from the session's WAKE or from each cycle's WAKE.

entries.title: Network homeostasis and state dynamics of neocortical sleep (Watson et al. 2016)
entries.description: Tests the findings of Watson, Levenstein, Greene, Gelinas and Buzsaki (2016) on both of the paper's datasets, DANDI:000041 (22 NWB files of spikes, LFP and Awake, Non-REM and REM states) and CRCNS:fcx-1 (the lab's 27 session folders with spikes, LFP, state intervals, UP/DOWN states, spindles and motion). It covers the data set's counts and state durations, firing rates by state, burst index, autocorrelograms, synchrony, UP/DOWN and spindle statistics, rate changes over sleep, within nonREM episodes and packets, and across sleep sub-state triplets.

entries.title: Firing rates across sleep states in rat frontal cortex (Watson et al. 2016)
entries.description: Tests the findings of Watson, Levenstein, Greene, Gelinas and Buzsaki (2016) on dandiset 000041, which holds silicon probe recordings of units, LFP and sleep states from the frontal cortex of 10 rats in their home cage. It compares firing rates and bursting across WAKE, nonREM and REM, how rates of fast and slow firing cells change over sleep and within nonREM packets, how they relate to LFP band power, and the rate changes across state triplets. UP and DOWN state and spindle analyses are blocked, as their methods are in the unavailable supplement.
